classification.difficultyReason: Combines circular counting, restrictions, opposite positions and a complement.

content.prompt: The letters A, E, I, P, Q and R are arranged in a circle. Find the probability that:

answer.worked:
All circular arrangements: $(6-1)!=5!=120$.

The vowels A, E and I form one unit. With consonants P, Q and R, there are four objects.

Circular arrangements of these objects: $(4-1)!=3!=6$.

Internal vowel arrangements: $3!=6$.

Acceptable arrangements: $6\times6=36$.

$$\begin{aligned}P&=\frac{36}{120}\\&=\frac{3}{10}.\end{aligned}$$

Fix A. R has one possible opposite position.

Arrange the remaining four letters: $4!=24$.

There are $(6-1)!=120$ circular arrangements in total.

$$\begin{aligned}P&=\frac{24}{120}\\&=\frac{1}{5}.\end{aligned}$$

There are three vowels, A, E and I, and three consonants, P, Q and R.

Fix one vowel. Arrange the other two vowels in alternate positions: $2!=2$.

Arrange the three consonants in the remaining positions: $3!=6$.

Acceptable arrangements: $2\times6=12$.

$$\begin{aligned}P&=\frac{12}{120}\\&=\frac{1}{10}.\end{aligned}$$

children.prompt: at least two vowels are next to one another.

answer.worked:
The complement is that no two vowels are adjacent. With three vowels and three consonants, this means they alternate, as in part c.

$$\begin{aligned}P&=1-\frac{1}{10}\\&=\frac{9}{10}.\end{aligned}$$
